mainTopic: A convert's earlier children (inheritance and פריה ורביה), and when the son of a לוייה or כהנת is exempt from פדיון הבן.
overview: This amud opens with the last line of an earlier discussion: the father's power of 'יכיר' is separate from ordinary face recognition. Then רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about a man who had sons as a גוי and then converted. רבי יוחנן says those earlier sons still count, so he has no new בכור for inheritance and he has already fulfilled פריה ורביה. ריש לקיש says 'גר שנתגייר כקטן שנולד', so the earlier sons do not count. The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן against a משנה and a ברייתא, assigning the ברייתא to רבי יוסי הגלילי. Next, רב אדא בר אהבה rules that a לוייה's firstborn son is exempt from פדיון הבן. רב פפא explains that the father was a גוי, while רבא explains that the father was a ישראל but פדיון depends on the mother's womb. A משנה about a כהנת seems to challenge רב פפא, and the גמרא answers that the 'כהנת' there is a בת ישראל whose son is a כהן.

steps.title: Closing line of the previous discussion: two different kinds of recognition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its second answer for רבי יוחנן from the previous עמוד. The 'recognition' (יכיר) needed for the בכור's inheritance is a separate standard from recognizing a face for testimony (הכרת פנים).
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule of 'יכיר' is one thing, and recognizing a face is a different thing.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of an earlier topic, not the start of a new one. The גמרא ends by saying two kinds of 'recognition' should not be mixed up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the בכור says only 'יכיר', 'he shall recognize', and does not mention the face. So for inheritance, seeing the forehead is enough recognition (Rashi). Testimony that a man died, so his wife may remarry, is different: there the witnesses must see the face with the nose. The two standards are separate, so the testimony rule is no challenge to רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He shall recognize' (דברים כא:יז). Here: the recognition the Torah needs to tell which twin is the בכור; since the פסוק does not say 'face', the forehead is enough (Rashi).
Separate; a different matter
Recognizing someone by his face

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the earlier sugya. Do not try to connect it to the convert dispute that comes next. The new topic starts with 'איתמר'.

phrases.english: "He shall recognize" is separate,
and recognition of the face is separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion from the previous daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For the בכור's inheritance, the forehead is enough for 'יכיר'. Identifying a dead man for testimony needs the face with the nose. The two standards are separate.

steps.title: New dispute: does a convert who already had children have a firstborn for inheritance?
steps.stepSummary: A man had sons as a גוי and then converted. רבי יוחנן says he has no בכור for inheritance. ריש לקיש says he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a man had sons while he was a non-Jew, and then he converted. רבי יוחנן says he has no בכור for inheritance purposes. רבי שמעון בן לקיש says he does have a בכור for inheritance purposes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new topic with 'איתמר' and presents a dispute between two אמוראים. The question is whether the first son born after the גירות gets the בכור's double portion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is the case. A man had children while he was a גוי, then converted, and then had another son. רבי יוחנן says that son does not get the double portion of a בכור. ריש לקיש says that son does get it. Their reasons come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: While he was a non-Jew
And he converted
A firstborn for inheritance, who takes a double portion

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about a convert's status runs through the rest of the sugya.

phrases.english: It was stated:
if he had sons while he was a gentile
and he then converted —
Rabbi Yochanan says:
he does not have a firstborn for inheritance,
and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
he does have a firstborn for inheritance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים בְּגַיּוּתוֹ וְנִתְגַּיֵּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: no בכור for inheritance after גירות. ריש לקיש: there is a בכור for inheritance after גירות.

steps.title: The reasons: 'first of his strength' versus 'a convert is like a newborn'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the man already had his 'ראשית אונו' before converting. ריש לקיש says a convert is like a newborn baby, so his past children do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he has no בכור for inheritance, because he already had his 'first of his strength'. ריש לקיש says he does have a בכור for inheritance, because a convert is like a newborn child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the reason behind each opinion from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה defines the בכור for inheritance as the father's 'ראשית אונו', his very first child. רבי יוחנן says the man's first child came while he was a גוי, so no later son can be 'first'. ריש לקיש says גירות gives a person a completely fresh start, like being born again, so his old children do not count and the first son after conversion is the real בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The first of his strength' (דברים כא:יז). The father's first child.
A convert is like a newborn child. Conversion is a total new beginning.
Because; since

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says the convert's earlier children still count. ריש לקיש says 'גר שנתגייר כקטן שנולד', so the earlier children do not count.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea 'גר שנתגייר כקטן שנולד' is a basic principle that appears all over ש״ס.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
he does not have a firstborn for inheritance —
because he already had "the first of his strength,"
and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
he does have a firstborn for inheritance —
a convert who converted is like a child just born.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind both sides of the dispute in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן relies on 'ראשית אונו' already happening before גירות. ריש לקיש relies on the principle 'גר שנתגייר כקטן שנולד'.

steps.title: They are consistent: the parallel dispute about פריה ורביה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש follow the same reasoning in another dispute. Has a convert who had children as a גוי already fulfilled פריה ורביה?
steps.simpleTranslation: They follow their own reasoning, as it was stated: a man had sons while a non-Jew and then converted. רבי יוחנן says he has fulfilled פריה ורביה. ריש לקיש says he has not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the same two אמוראים argue in the same direction about a second law. The question there is whether the convert has already done the מצוה of having children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ואזדו לטעמייהו' means each אמורא is being consistent. רבי יוחנן says children born before the גירות still count, so they count toward פריה ורביה too. ריש לקיש says those children do not count, so the man must have children again as a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They follow their own reasoning.' Each one is consistent with his view elsewhere.
The מצוה to be fruitful and multiply
He fulfilled (the מצוה)

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning,
as it was stated:
if he had sons while a gentile and then converted —

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: קִיֵּים פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: he has fulfilled being fruitful and multiplying,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לֹא קִיֵּים.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: he has not fulfilled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the inheritance dispute to a parallel dispute and shows that both sides are consistent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: a convert who had children as a גוי has fulfilled פריה ורביה. ריש לקיש: he has not.

steps.title: Reasons in the פריה ורביה dispute: 'made to be inhabited' versus 'like a newborn'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes 'לא תהו בראה לשבת יצרה': the man has already helped fill the world. ריש לקיש again says a convert is like a newborn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he fulfilled it, based on the פסוק 'He did not create it to be empty; He formed it to be lived in.' ריש לקיש says he did not fulfill פריה ורביה, because a convert is like a newborn child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for each side in the פריה ורביה dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads the מצוה through the פסוק in ישעיה. The goal of the מצוה is to fill the world with people. Children born before the גירות really exist and really fill the world, so the goal was reached. ריש לקיש uses the same principle as before: after גירות the man is a new person, so his earlier children do not count.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He did not create it to be empty; He formed it to be inhabited' (ישעיה מה:יח)
Inhabiting; settling the world

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש uses the same reason, 'כקטן שנולד', in both disputes. רבי יוחנן uses a different reason in each: 'ראשית אונו' for inheritance and 'לשבת יצרה' for פריה ורביה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: he has fulfilled it —
"He did not create it to be a waste; He formed it to be inhabited,"
and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
he has not fulfilled being fruitful and multiplying —
a convert who converted is like a child just born.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind both sides of the dispute in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן bases his view on 'לשבת יצרה': the world is already more inhabited. ריש לקיש bases his view on 'גר שנתגייר כקטן שנולד'.

steps.title: Why both disputes had to be recorded: the first half of the explanation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why it needed both disputes. Had we heard only the inheritance case, we might think ריש לקיש would agree with רבי יוחנן about פריה ורביה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are necessary. If only the first case had been stated, we would say ריש לקיש rules that way only there, because non-Jews are not subject to the Torah's inheritance laws. But in the פריה ורביה case, one might say he agrees with רבי יוחנן, since the פסוק says 'He formed it to be inhabited', and this man did help inhabit the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why record the same dispute twice? It explains that ריש לקיש's view in the inheritance case alone would not have taught us his view on פריה ורביה. The other half of the explanation continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the inheritance case, ריש לקיש has an extra reason. A גוי's children were never under the Torah's inheritance laws, such as the double portion of the בכור, so of course they do not count. With פריה ורביה, the goal is simply to populate the world, and that has happened regardless of religion. So we might have thought ריש לקיש agrees there. That is why his opinion had to be stated in that case too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is necessary.' Explains why two similar statements were both needed.
In this first case
They are not subject to the laws of inheritance
One might say he agrees with him

steps.confusionAlert: 'אבל בהא אימא מודה' is a 'might have thought'. It is NOT ריש לקיש's real view. He really holds 'לא קיים'. The צריכא only shows why we needed to be told that.

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for if it had been stated only in this first case,

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: in this case Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says his view,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דִּבְגַיּוּתָן לָאו בְּנֵי נַחֲלָה נִינְהוּ,
phrases.english: because in their gentile state they are not subject to inheritance,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהָא אֵימָא מוֹדֶה לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: but in that case, say that he agrees with Rabbi Yochanan,
since "He did not create it to be a waste; He formed it to be inhabited,"
and this man has made it inhabited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the implied question of why both parallel disputes from steps 2 and 4 needed to be recorded.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: showing that each statement teaches something the other does not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the inheritance case alone, we might think ריש לקיש agrees with רבי יוחנן about פריה ורביה, since the world has been populated.
steps.terutzMaskana: So the פריה ורביה dispute had to be stated to show that ריש לקיש holds 'לא קיים' there too. The other half of the צריכא continues next.

steps.title: The other side of why both disputes were needed
steps.stepSummary: Had we heard the dispute only about פריה ורביה, we might think רבי יוחנן holds his view only there, and agrees with ריש לקיש about inheritance. So both disputes had to be stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had been said only in this case (פריה ורביה), [we would say that] in this case רבי יוחנן says [his view], but in that case (inheritance), say he agrees with ריש לקיש. So it is necessary [to state both].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation it began in step 6 about why both disputes are recorded. It now gives the reverse side and closes with the word צריכא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 we saw that the inheritance case alone would not have told us ריש לקיש's view on פריה ורביה. Here we see that the פריה ורביה case alone would not tell us רבי יוחנן's view on inheritance. For פריה ורביה, רבי יוחנן has a special verse (לא תהו בראה) about filling the world, so we might have thought he would agree with ריש לקיש about inheritance, where no such verse applies.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. Both statements are needed because each teaches something new.
If it had been stated. Introduces a 'what if we had only heard one case' argument.
Agrees, concedes

steps.whatToRemember: Both disputes are needed. Each אמורא's view in one case could not be guessed from the other case, because each case has its own reasoning.

phrases.english: And if it had been stated only in this case,
phrases.notes: The case of פריה ורביה

phrases.english: [we would say that] in this case Rabbi Yochanan says [his view],
phrases.notes: Because of the verse לא תהו בראה

phrases.english: but in that case, I would say
phrases.notes: The case of inheritance

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: he agrees with Reish Lakish.
phrases.notes: Children from before conversion would not count

phrases.english: Therefore it is necessary [to state both].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the צריכותא begun in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows that each of the two parallel disputes teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the פריה ורביה case, one might think רבי יוחנן agrees with ריש לקיש about inheritance.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both disputes are recorded so we know each אמורא holds his view in both areas.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about a mother who gave birth after converting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה: a man with no sons marries a woman who already gave birth, or who gave birth while still a maidservant or a גויה. A child she bears after joining the Jewish people is a בכור for inheritance but not a בכור for the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: One who had no sons and married a woman who had already given birth; [or a woman who gave birth while] still a maidservant and was then freed; [or while] still a גויה and then converted; and after she came into the Jewish people she gave birth. Her child is a בכור for inheritance but not a בכור for the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against רבי יוחנן by quoting a משנה. This step only sets up the source; the actual problem is drawn out in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new child is not a בכור for the כהן, because that kind of בכור depends on the mother, and she already gave birth. But he is a בכור for inheritance, which depends on the father being a first-time father. The גמרא will now ask who this father is, to see whether the משנה fits רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish maidservant (שפחה כנענית)
She was freed
A firstborn for inheritance, who gets a double portion. Depends on the father.
A firstborn who must be redeemed from a כהן. Depends on the mother.

steps.confusionAlert: There are two kinds of בכור. A בכור for the כהן depends on the mother's first birth. A בכור for inheritance depends on the father's first child. One child can be a בכור in one sense and not in the other.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: מִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים,
phrases.english: We learned: One who did not have sons,
and he married a woman who had already given birth;
[or she gave birth] while still a maidservant and was then freed;
[or she gave birth] while still a gentile and then converted;
and after she came into the Jewish people she gave birth —
phrases.notes: To a male child

phrases.english: her child is a firstborn for inheritance
but is not a firstborn for the priest.
phrases.notes: Because she already gave birth before

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: מִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the צריכותא, the גמרא turns to test רבי יוחנן's view against a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a convert who had sons as a גוי has no בכור for inheritance
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The setup: the משנה rules that a child born after the mother joined the Jewish people is a בכור for inheritance. The next steps will show the father must be a convert who already had sons.

steps.title: Who is the father? Not an ordinary Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who fathered this child. If it was a Jew with no prior sons, why mention a freed maidservant or convert? The same law would apply even with a Jewish mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: She gave birth from whom? If you say from a Jew who had no sons, why mention specifically a convert and a maidservant? Even a Jewish woman would be the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the father is in the משנה's case and rules out the obvious answer. This prepares the next step, where it names the only father who makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inheritance-בכור depends only on the father. If the father is a Jew with no sons, his first son is a בכור for inheritance even if the mother is a Jewish woman who had children before. So mentioning a convert or freed maidservant would teach nothing new. The extra detail must point to a different kind of father.

keyTerms.meaning: From whom?
If you say. Introduces a possible answer the גמרא will reject.
Why specifically this case? Used when a detail seems unnecessary.
A female convert

phrases.english: She gave birth from whom?
phrases.notes: Who is the father?

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵימָא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים —
phrases.english: If you say from a Jew who had no sons —
phrases.notes: The man mentioned at the start of the משנה

phrases.english: why mention specifically a convert and a maidservant?
Even a Jewish woman would be the same!
phrases.notes: Since the father's status alone decides inheritance

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the משנה just quoted to find out who the father is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the father in the משנה's case of the freed maidservant or convert
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First option rejected: it cannot be an ordinary Jew without sons, because then mentioning a convert or maidservant would be pointless.

steps.title: The father must be a convert who had sons, a challenge to רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: So the father must be a convert who had sons as a גוי. The משנה still calls the child a בכור for inheritance, which contradicts רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not from a convert who had sons and then converted? And the משנה teaches that [the child] is a בכור for inheritance!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes the father must be a convert who already had sons as a גוי. It then points out that the משנה calls the child a בכור for inheritance, which challenges רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mention of a convert or maidservant mother shows the father is like her, a convert who had children before converting. According to רבי יוחנן, this man already had his ראשית אונו, so a new son should not be a בכור for inheritance. The משנה says he is, which matches ריש לקיש's view that a convert is like a newborn.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? Introduces the only remaining explanation, which leads to the challenge.
And it teaches. Points to what the משנה explicitly says.
A male convert

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a direct challenge from a משנה to רבי יוחנן. An אמורא cannot argue with a משנה, so the גמרא will need to find an answer for him.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not from a convert
who had sons and then converted?
phrases.notes: Sons born while he was a גוי

phrases.english: And it teaches that he is a firstborn for inheritance!
phrases.notes: Against רבי יוחנן

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו מִגֵּר שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים וְנִתְגַּיֵּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out an ordinary Jewish father in step 9, the גמרא names the remaining option and draws the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that a convert who had sons as a גוי has no בכור for inheritance
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's case must involve a convert father who already had sons as a גוי. The משנה calls his new son a בכור for inheritance, contradicting רבי יוחנן and supporting ריש לקיש.

steps.title: The father is a Jew with no sons; the mother's status matters only for the כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is about a Jewish father with no prior sons. It mentions a convert or maidservant mother only for the second half: the child is not a בכור for the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, the child is from a Jew who had no sons. The משנה needed to mention a convert or maidservant mother for the words "he is not a בכור for the כהן."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the claim from step 10 that the father must be a convert. It says the father is an ordinary Jew with no sons, so the משנה no longer contradicts רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 asked why the משנה would mention a convert or maidservant mother if the father is a Jew with no sons. The answer is that the mother's history matters for the second law, not the first. A Jewish father with no sons gives a בכור for inheritance no matter who the mother is. But whether the child is a בכור for the כהן depends on whether the mother already gave birth, even as a non-Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (the גמרא is restating the case)
A firstborn who must be redeemed from a כהן (פדיון הבן)
It was needed for it

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different kinds of בכור. The בכור for inheritance depends on the FATHER (his first son). The בכור for the כהן depends on the MOTHER (the first to open her womb). Keep them apart.

phrases.english: No; actually, it is from a Jew
who had no sons,
and it was needed for the clause "he is not a firstborn for the priest."
phrases.notes: So the משנה mentions a mother who is a convert or maidservant just for the sake of the כהן part.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 by redefining the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case (לעולם): the father is a Jew, and the convert detail serves a different clause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father must be a convert who had sons as a גוי, which would contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father is a Jew with no sons. The mother's background is mentioned only for the law that the child is not a בכור for the כהן.

steps.title: The משנה is excluding the view of רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The clause "not a בכור for the כהן" comes to reject רבי יוסי הגלילי. He holds that births before conversion do not count, so the child would be a בכור for the כהן too.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes to exclude רבי יוסי הגלילי. He says the child is a בכור both for inheritance and for the כהן, because the verse says "opens the womb in Israel," meaning only when he opens the womb of a Jewish woman. The משנה teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the clause "not a בכור for the כהן" needed to be taught. It is there to argue against רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads "פטר רחם בישראל" to mean that only a birth from a Jewish woman counts as opening the womb. So, in his view, children born while she was a non-Jew are ignored, and her first child after conversion is a בכור for the כהן. Our משנה disagrees: her womb was already opened before she converted, so this child is not a בכור for the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude (a different opinion)
The one who opens the womb (the first birth)
It teaches us

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key point for the next steps. רבי יוסי הגלילי ignores children born before conversion, and this is the opinion the גמרא will use to explain the ברייתא.

phrases.english: to exclude the view of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
who says: he is a firstborn for inheritance and for the priest,
as it is stated: "opens the womb in Israel" —

steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the purpose of a clause (לאפוקי).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might follow רבי יוסי הגלילי and say births before conversion are ignored, making the child a בכור for the כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה rules that the child is not a בכור for the כהן, because her womb was already opened.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a convert with sons from before conversion has a בכור for inheritance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a man who had sons as a גוי and then converted has a בכור for inheritance. This seems to contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he had sons when he was a גוי and then converted, he has a בכור for inheritance!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source against רבי יוחנן. This ברייתא clearly speaks about a convert father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא could escape by saying the father was a Jew. Here the ברייתא says outright that the father had sons as a גוי. It still says his first son after conversion is a בכור for inheritance, which goes against רבי יוחנן's view that sons from before conversion do count.

keyTerms.meaning: When he was a non-Jew
He converted

phrases.english: Come and hear:
if he had sons while he was a gentile and then converted,
he has a firstborn for inheritance!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים בְּגַיּוּתוֹ וְנִתְגַּיֵּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה was explained away, a new and clearer source is brought against רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן, who holds that a convert's sons from before conversion count, so he has no new בכור for inheritance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly speaks of a convert father and still gives him a בכור for inheritance. So there is no way to say the father was a Jew.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רבינא (or רב אחא) answers that this ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. He ignores births before conversion and applies the same idea to the father. רבי יוחנן can follow the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said, and some say it was רב אחא: this is surely רבי יוסי הגלילי. He says "opens the womb in Israel" means only a birth from a Jewish woman, and he learns the father's law from the mother's law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ברייתא is following רבי יוסי הגלילי, so it does not bind רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a mother, רבי יוסי הגלילי ignores births from before her conversion. He applies the same rule to a father, so a convert's sons from before conversion are ignored and his next son is a בכור for inheritance. רבי יוחנן can simply follow the חכמים who disagree with רבי יוסי הגלילי, as our משנה does.

keyTerms.meaning: This is certainly
And he learns his (the father's) law from hers (the mother's)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן survives both challenges. The משנה is about a Jewish father, and the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, whom the משנה itself rejects.

who says "opens the womb in Israel" —

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אַחָא: הָא וַדַּאי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הִוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by assigning the ברייתא to a minority opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a specific תנא (הא מני).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is a general rule that contradicts רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. רבי יוחנן follows the חכמים, who count sons from before conversion.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: the son of a לוייה is exempt from five סלעים
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins. רב אדא בר אהבה rules that when a לוייה gives birth to a firstborn son, he is exempt from the five סלעים of פדיון הבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: a לוייה who gave birth, her son is exempt from the five סלעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ruling from רב אדא בר אהבה. This sets up the next question about who the father is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a firstborn son must be redeemed from a כהן with five סלעים. לויים are exempt from this. רב אדא בר אהבה says the son of a לוייה is also exempt, but he does not say who the father is. That gap is what the גמרא asks about next.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman from the tribe of לוי
Exempt
Five סלעים, the payment to a כהן for פדיון הבן

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
a Levite woman who gave birth —
her son is exempt from the five sela coins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: לְוִיָּיה שֶׁיָּלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about פדיון הבן after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The firstborn son of a לוייה is exempt from paying five סלעים to a כהן.

steps.title: Who is the father? If he is a כהן or a לוי, why mention a לוייה at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whom the לוייה became pregnant from. If the father is a כהן or a לוי, then even an ordinary Jewish woman's son would be exempt, so why say לוייה?
steps.simpleTranslation: From whom did she become pregnant? If you say from a כהן or a לוי, why specifically a לוייה? Even an ordinary Jewish woman too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the father is in רב אדא בר אהבה's case. It rejects the first possibility, a כהן or לוי father, and so sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child of a כהן or לוי father is exempt no matter who the mother is. If that were the case, mentioning that the mother is a לוייה would add nothing. So the case must be one where the mother's being a לוייה is what makes the son exempt. The גמרא will explain this next.

keyTerms.meaning: From whom did she become pregnant?
If you say (introduces a suggestion about to be rejected)

An ordinary Jewish woman (not כהן or לוי)

If we say she became pregnant from a priest or a Levite,

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the father of the son of the לוייה in רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling?
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the father is a כהן or לוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the father were a כהן or לוי, the mother's tribe would not matter. Mentioning a לוייה would then be pointless.

steps.title: If the father is a regular Jew, lineage should follow him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the last option: the לוייה became pregnant from a ישראל. It rejects this right away, because the פסוק says family lineage follows the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, she became pregnant from a ישראל? But it is written: "By their families, by their fathers' houses"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the question from step 16. The father cannot be a כהן or לוי, so maybe he is a regular ישראל. But that does not work either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "למשפחותם לבית אבותם" teaches that a child's tribe follows the father. If the father is a ישראל, the son is a ישראל and should owe פדיון הבן. So the mother being a לוייה should not matter, and רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling still makes no sense.

by their families, by their fathers' houses (lineage follows the father)
it is written

phrases.english: Rather, where she became pregnant from an Israelite,
phrases.notes: The third possible father, after a כהן and a לוי.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lineage follows the father. A ישראל father makes the son a ישראל, so he should owe פדיון הבן.

steps.title: The father was a non-Jew, so the child counts as a לוי
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the לוייה became pregnant from a גוי. The child follows the mother and is a לוי, so he is exempt. This holds even according to the view that such a child is flawed: he is still a לוי, just a 'flawed לוי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: She became pregnant from a גוי. Do not say this works only for the view that we do not taint the child. Even for the view that we do taint the child, he is called a flawed לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא solves the puzzle with a fourth option: the father was a גוי. A child of a גוי father and a Jewish mother follows the mother, so here he is a לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'by their fathers' houses' only applies when the father is Jewish. With a גוי father, the child takes his mother's status, and a לוי is exempt from פדיון הבן. There is a מחלוקת about whether such a child is 'tainted' (flawed in lineage). רב פפא says that even if he is flawed, he is still a לוי, so he is still exempt.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the father had to be Jewish, so his status would decide the child's.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father is a גוי, so the child follows his לוייה mother. He is a לוי, even if a flawed one, and is exempt from the five סלעים.

steps.title: The father was a ישראל, but פדיון הבן depends on the womb
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרב יוסף, in the name of רבא, gives a different answer. The father really was a ישראל. But פדיון הבן is different, because the תורה ties it to 'opening the womb', and this womb belongs to a לוייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרב יוסף said in the name of רבא: Really, she became pregnant from a ישראל. But there it is different, because the verse says "opens the womb". The Merciful One made it depend on the opening of the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second, separate answer to the question. It keeps the simple case, a ישראל father, and explains why the son is still exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is true that the child is a ישראל, because his tribe follows the father. But the obligation of פדיון הבן is defined by 'פטר רחם', the opening of the womb. So the mother is what counts here, and a לוייה's womb is exempt. This answer explains the exemption from the mother, without changing the child's tribe.

steps.title: A משנה is quoted to challenge רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge to רב פפא. It quotes our משנה about a woman who converted while pregnant, or a slave woman freed while pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: One who had sons and married a woman who had not given birth; a woman who converted while pregnant; a woman who was freed while pregnant...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes a משנה whose cases look like they conflict with רב פפא's idea. The actual question will be spelled out right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that in these cases the son is a בכור for the כהן (he must be redeemed) but not a בכור for inheritance. These opening cases are quoted only to set up the passage. The challenge to רב פפא comes from the next clause, about a baby mixed up with the baby of a כהנת or a לוייה (steps 21-24).

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים וְנָשָׂא אִשָּׁה שֶׁלֹּא יָלָדָה

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's later clause, about a mix-up with a כהנת's or a לוייה's baby, implies that their sons are exempt. A כהן or לוי father would make the mother's tribe irrelevant. A גוי father, which is רב פפא's approach, fails for a כהנת, because she becomes a זרה (steps 22-28).

steps.title: The rest of the משנה being used to challenge רב פפא

steps.title: Inference from the משנה and the question of who the father was
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה we learn that the sons of a כהנת and a לוייה are exempt. The גמרא asks whom these women became pregnant from.

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from the משנה: a כהנת's and a לוייה's sons are exempt from פדיון הבן. Then it asks who the father was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only makes sense if the other woman's son is exempt. That is why the mix-up creates a doubt for our woman's son. To understand why he is exempt, the גמרא needs to know the father's identity.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who the father is in the משנה's case of a כהנת or לוייה whose son is exempt.

steps.title: The father cannot be a כהן or לוי
steps.stepSummary: If the father was a כהן or a לוי, the mother's tribe would not matter. Even a בת ישראל's son from such a father would be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say she became pregnant from a כהן or a לוי, then why mention specifically a כהנת and a לוייה? Even a בת ישראל would also be the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, that the father was a כהן or a לוי, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tribe follows the father, so a כהן's or לוי's son is exempt no matter who his mother is. Then the משנה should not have picked a כהנת or a לוייה. Since it did, the mother's tribe must be what matters. This is the same reasoning we saw in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say
Why specifically this case?
An ordinary Jewish woman (not from כהנים or לויים)

phrases.english: If you say she became pregnant from a priest or a Levite,

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי מַאי אִירְיָא כֹּהֶנֶת וּלְוִיָּה?
phrases.english: if so, why specifically a priest's daughter and a Levite's daughter?
Even an Israelite woman would also be exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the first possible answer to step 22's question and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that the father was a כהן or a לוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the father decides the exemption, then naming the mother's tribe is pointless.

steps.title: If the father was a גוי, is a כהנת's son really exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The only option left is that the father was a גוי, which matches רב פפא's approach. But that is a problem: is a כהנת's son from a גוי really exempt? רב פפא himself reported that רבה raised this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, she became pregnant from a גוי. Is a כהנת then exempt? But רב פפא said: רבה tested us: a כהנת who became pregnant from a גוי, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the father must have been a גוי, like רב פפא answered earlier. Then it challenges this: it is not clear that a כהנת's son from a גוי is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a גוי father, the child follows the mother. That works well for a לוייה. But the משנה also lists a כהנת, and רב פפא's own report ends with רבה ruling that a כהנת becomes 'זרה' through a גוי, so her son is not exempt. So the משנה seems to clash with רב פפא's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew
But didn't [so-and-so] say? (introduces a contradicting source)
He tested us
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rather, she became pregnant from a gentile;
is a priest's daughter exempt?
But didn't Rav Pappa say:
Rabba tested us:
A priest's daughter who became pregnant from a gentile, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting a כהן or לוי father, the גמרא moves to a גוי father and finds a difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's view that a mother's tribe passes to her son from a גוי, applied to the כהנת in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies a כהנת's son from a גוי is exempt, but רבה ruled that a כהנת's son from a גוי is obligated, and רב פפא himself reports it.

steps.title: רב פפא compares the כהנת to רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answered רבה that this is the same as רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling: a לוייה's son is exempt from the five סלעים. That ruling refers to a גוי father.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I said to him: Isn't this the same as רב אדא בר אהבה, who said: a לוייה who gave birth, her son is exempt from five סלעים?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא continues his story: he told רבה that the כהנת case is just like the לוייה case of רב אדא בר אהבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה ruled that a לוייה's son from a גוי is exempt, because the child follows the mother. רב פפא assumed a כהנת works the same way, so her son should also be exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: And I said to him
Isn't this the same as
The five silver coins given to a כהן for פדיון הבן

phrases.english: And I said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו הַיְינוּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה,
phrases.english: Isn't this the ruling of Rav Adda bar Ahava,
who said: A Levite's daughter who gave birth,
her son is exempt from the five sela coins?
phrases.notes: Understood as a case where the father was a גוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמֵינָא לֵיהּ: לָאו הַיְינוּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב פפא's report: his answer to רבה's test question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כהנת is like a לוייה: her son from a גוי follows her and is exempt, just as רב אדא בר אהבה ruled about a לוייה.

steps.title: רבה rejects the comparison: a לוייה keeps her holiness
steps.stepSummary: רבה told רב פפא that the two cases cannot be compared. A לוייה stays in her holy status even after relations with a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said to me: How can you compare? It makes sense for a לוייה, because she stays in her holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes back on רב פפא's comparison. He starts explaining why a לוייה is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה agrees about the לוייה, because her status is not damaged by what happened, so her son can inherit her לוי status. The word בשלמא ('it makes sense for…') signals that a contrast with the כהנת is coming. That contrast is given in step 28.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare?! (rejecting a comparison)
It makes sense for [this case] (a contrast follows)
She remains in her holiness

phrases.english: And he said to me: How can you compare?!
It makes sense for a Levite's daughter, since she remains in her sanctity,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבה rejects רב פפא's answer from step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between a כהנת and a לוייה, not רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A לוייה's holiness survives relations with a גוי, and the כהנת may not share this, so the two cases are not the same.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not disagreeing about the לוייה. He accepts that a לוייה's son is exempt. He only denies that a כהנת is the same.

steps.title: ברייתא: a captured or violated לוייה still eats מעשר
steps.stepSummary: רבה brings a ברייתא as proof. A לוייה who was captured, or who had forbidden relations, is still given מעשר ראשון and may eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: a לוייה who was captured, or who had relations of זנות, is given מעשר and eats it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה proves from a ברייתא that a לוייה keeps her holy status even after forbidden relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in the worst case, definite זנות, she keeps her right to מעשר, which belongs to לויים. This shows her לוי status is not damaged. That is why her son from a גוי can still count as a לוי for פדיון הבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Who was taken captive
Forbidden, promiscuous relations
Here, מעשר ראשון, the tithe given to לויים

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
A Levite's daughter who was taken captive
or who engaged in licentious intercourse,
they give her from the tithe and she eats it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה's claim in step 26 that a לוייה stays in her holiness.
steps.raayaObject: That a לוייה's holy status survives captivity or זנות
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling that such a לוייה still receives and eats מעשר
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the coming contrast. A כהנת who has relations with a גוי may lose her status, for example her right to eat תרומה. If so, her son would not be exempt, and that is the problem for רב פפא.

steps.title: A כהנת loses her status after relations with a גוי
steps.stepSummary: רבה completes his distinction. Unlike a לוייה, a כהנת who has relations with a גוי becomes a זרה, so her son from a גוי should not be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a כהנת is different: once a גוי has relations with her, she becomes a זרה (a non-כהן woman, no longer allowed to eat תרומה).
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes explaining why the case of a לוייה does not prove anything about a כהנת. A כהנת loses her special status after relations with a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לוייה stays a לוייה even after forbidden relations, as the ברייתא about מעשר ראשון showed. A כהנת, however, becomes disqualified from תרומה, so she is treated like a regular בת ישראל. Her son from a גוי should therefore need פדיון, and רב פפא's reading of the משנה falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter of a כהן
He has relations with her
A non-כהן woman, who may not eat תרומה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two women. A לוייה keeps her status (she can still eat מעשר ראשון). A כהנת loses hers (she can no longer eat תרומה). This difference is the whole point of רבה's rejection.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כֹּהֶנֶת, כֵּיוָן דְּאִי בָּעֵיל לַהּ,
phrases.english: But a priest's daughter, since if [a gentile] has relations with her,
phrases.notes: The subject is a גוי, carried over from the previous steps.

phrases.english: she becomes a non-priestess!
phrases.notes: She is disqualified from eating תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כֹּהֶנֶת, כֵּיוָן דְּאִי בָּעֵיל לַהּ, הָוְיָא זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 27 to finish the contrast. A לוייה keeps her status, but a כהנת does not.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב פפא's answer from step 25, which compared a כהנת to רב אדא בר אהבה's case of a לוייה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison fails because a כהנת becomes a זרה after relations with a גוי, while a לוייה stays holy.
steps.whyThisMatters: Once this distinction stands, the 'גוי father' reading of the משנה is gone. The גמרא now has to find a different case for the exempt כהנת's son.

steps.title: Fine for מר בריה דרב יוסף, but how does רב פפא explain the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרב יוסף can say the משנה means a כהנת pregnant from a ישראל. רב פפא holds that such a son needs פדיון, so what case does he think the משנה means?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for מר בריה דרב יוסף, who said in the name of רבא that the case is where she became pregnant from a ישראל. He can explain the משנה as a case where she became pregnant from a ישראל. But according to רב פפא, how does he explain the משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא. Every option for explaining the משנה seems to be blocked for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בריה דרב יוסף holds that a כהנת's or לוייה's son from a ישראל father is exempt. So for him, the משנה is easy. רב פפא holds that this son is obligated, and the 'גוי father' option was just rejected in step 28. So רב פפא seems to have no case left for the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one opinion)
She became pregnant
He explains it as referring to (a specific case)
In what (case)?

phrases.english: This works well for Mar, son of Rav Yosef,
in the name of Rava, who said [the case is] where she became pregnant from an Israelite,
phrases.notes: This is his explanation of רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling about a לוייה.

phrases.english: he can explain it [the mishna] as where she became pregnant from an Israelite;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַב פָּפָּא בְּמַאי מוֹקֵי לָהּ?
phrases.english: but according to Rav Pappa, how does he explain it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 28 removed the 'גוי father' option. Now the גמרא asks what case is left for רב פפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's ability to explain the משנה that exempts a כהנת's son
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ישראל father does not work for רב פפא (he holds the son is obligated). A גוי father was just rejected. A כהן or לוי father would make the mother's tribe irrelevant (step 23). So nothing seems to fit.

steps.title: The mother is a בת ישראל who became pregnant from a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה differently. The case is a regular בת ישראל who became pregnant from a כהן, so her son is a כהן and exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the case is where she became pregnant from a כהן, and she herself is a בת ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב פפא by changing what 'כהנת' in the משנה means. The father is a כהן, and the mother is a regular בת ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב פפא, when the father is Jewish, the son's tribe follows the father ('לבית אבותם'). A son of a כהן is a כהן, so he is exempt from פדיון. This avoids every problem raised before, because the mother is not actually a כהנת at all. The לוייה in the משנה can still be one who became pregnant from a גוי, as רב פפא said, since a לוייה keeps her holiness (Rashi).

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (signals a new reading of the case)
A regular Jewish woman, not from a כהן or לוי family

phrases.english: Actually, it is where she became pregnant from a priest,
and she is an Israelite woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 29 by redefining the case in the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed 'כהנת' meant a woman born to a כהן family, which left רב פפא with no workable case.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כהנת' means a בת ישראל pregnant from a כהן. Her son is a כהן through his father and is exempt.

steps.title: Why does the משנה call her a כהנת?
steps.stepSummary: If she is really a בת ישראל, why does the משנה use the word 'כהנת'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does the משנה call her a 'כהנת'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a wording question about its own new answer. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reading creates a problem with the wording. A בת ישראל is not normally called a כהנת. The גמרא needs to explain the משנה's word choice.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Calls her

phrases.english: And why does it call her a 'kohenet'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the wording of the משנה fits the new case given in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a בת ישראל would be called 'כהנת' in the משנה

steps.title: She is called כהנת because her son is a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה calls her 'כהנת' because of her son, who is a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because her son is a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the wording. The mother gets the title 'כהנת' because of her son's status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The title here comes from her son, not from her own family. Since she is the mother of a כהן, the משנה can call her a כהנת. This fully saves רב פפא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Her son

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, the exempt 'כהנת' in the משנה is a בת ישראל who had a son from a כהן. The son is exempt because he is a כהן. She is called 'כהנת' only because of him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the challenge against רב פפא. His view, that a Jewish father decides the son's tribe and only with a גוי father does the son follow his mother, now fits the משנה.

phrases.english: Because her son is a priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is called 'כהנת' because her son is a כהן.
